issues.description: In the solution repository, PersonService.deletePerson has the signature deletePerson(Person person) but the REST controller (PersonResource) calls personService.deletePerson(personId) passing a UUID. The template PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId). This parameter-type mismatch between PersonService and its caller (PersonResource) will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the intended API (delete by UUID). The problem statement and template describe DELETE /persons/{personId} which implies deletion by UUID, so the service should accept a UUID.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the PersonService.deletePerson method signature consistent with the REST API and template by accepting a UUID (deletePerson(UUID personId)) and implement removal by comparing person.getId() to the given UUID. Alternatively, update PersonResource to obtain a Person instance before calling deletePerson(Person) — but the clearer fix is to change PersonService to deletePerson(UUID) so service and controller agree and match the problem statement.

issues.description: Inconsistent signature/name for the delete-person operation across artifacts: the Problem Statement and server-side endpoints describe DELETE /persons/{personId} (i.e., an ID-based delete). The template PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId) (ID parameter) while the solution's PersonService declares deletePerson(Person person) (Person parameter). Meanwhile the solution's PersonResource invokes personService.deletePerson(personId) (passing UUID). This mismatch between expecting an ID and providing a Person object creates confusion for students mapping the DELETE endpoint to the service method and can lead to compilation or implementation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the deletePerson API consistent across artifacts by using an ID-based delete everywhere. Change the service method in the solution to public void deletePerson(UUID personId) (matching the template and the DELETE /persons/{personId} endpoint) and implement removal by comparing IDs. Ensure PersonResource calls personService.deletePerson(personId).
